pages.title: What this unit is about
pages.body:
> 🌐 **Strand 3 — Communication Networks**
Sub-strand 4: Web Technologies

A search engine can return millions of results in less than a second, but finding the right ones takes skill. In this unit you will learn search techniques and compare different search engines.

pages.title: Content standard and lessons
pages.body:
> 🎯 **Content standard**

pages.title: Effective Search Techniques
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B8.3.4.1.1
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- identify effective search techniques;
- search with single and combined techniques.
| **Technique** | **Example search** | **Effect** |
|---|---|---|
| Use specific keywords with exact spelling | causes of malaria Ghana | Better than a long question; correct spelling gives relevant results |
| Phrase search with quotation marks | "Kwame Nkrumah Mausoleum" | Finds the exact phrase in that order |
| AND | cocoa AND Ghana | Both words must appear (most engines do this automatically) |
| OR (capital letters) | cocoa OR coffee | Either word: widens the search |
| NOT or minus sign | jaguar NOT car / jaguar -car | Excludes a word (Google uses the minus sign) |
| site: | BECE timetable site:waecgh.org | Searches only one website or domain (e.g. site:.gov.gh) |
| filetype: | computing curriculum filetype:pdf | Finds a particular file type |
| intitle: | intitle:robotics | The word must be in the page title |
| Wildcard ∗ | "the ∗ of Ghana" | The ∗ stands for any word |
| Tools / filters | Images, News, Videos; date ranges | Use the menu under the search box |
[[fig:c8-f17|Figure 16: How AND, OR and NOT change search results]]
> 💻 **Practical session — Combine techniques**
Search for Ghana’s independence history using: (1) a plain question; (2) "Ghana independence" 1957 site:.gov.gh; (3) "Ghana independence" -football filetype:pdf. Record the number of results and the quality of the top three for each. Which search worked best?

pages.title: Using More Than One Search Engine
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B8.3.4.1.2
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- investigate different search engines;
- compare results for the same search terms;
- discuss the findings.
| **Search engine** | **Notes** |
|---|---|
| Google | The most widely used; large index; many tools |
| Microsoft Bing | Second largest; powers several other engines; integrated with Microsoft Copilot |
| Yahoo! Search | Results largely provided by Bing |
| DuckDuckGo | Focuses on privacy: does not track users or personalise results |
| Ask.com | Originally a question-and-answer search engine |
| Ecosia | Uses advertising income to plant trees |
> 🧪 **Activity — Search engine investigation**
In groups, type the **same search string** (e.g. best ways to manage e-waste in Ghana) into three search engines. Record: (a) the number of results if shown, (b) the top five websites, (c) adverts or sponsored results, (d) how many results are Ghanaian sources. Discuss why results differ: different indexes, ranking algorithms, personalisation, location and advertising.
